clues: This city sits in the valleys of three rivers, in a desert on the central coast of its land. It looks out over the Pacific Ocean.
This desert city stays mild, though it lies in the hot tropics. Cold sea water close by cools the air, and rain is very rare here.
A Spanish captain picked this river valley for his new capital and founded the city in 1535. It soon ruled a vast realm for Spain.
This city was founded in 1535 with a grand name: City of the Kings. The name marked a feast day in early January, when the city was founded.
This city is the political and trade heart of Peru. The Government Palace, first built by its founder, stands here still.
